message.content:
I’m happy to help!  
Here’s a quick rundown of the major Canadian public holidays in 2023 that typically create long‑weekend opportunities (i.e., holidays falling on weekdays that give you an extra day off).  

| Date | Holiday | Day of Week | Typical Long Weekend |
|------|---------|-------------|---------------------|
| Jan 1 | New Year’s Day | Sun | No extra day (but many people take a day off) |
| Apr 7 | Good Friday | Fri | Yes – Fri–Sat (or Fri–Mon if you take Monday off) |
| May 22 | Victoria Day | Mon | Yes – Sat–Mon |
| Jul 1 | Canada Day | Tue | Yes – Mon–Tue (or Tue–Wed if you take Monday off) |
| Sep 18 | Labour Day | Mon | Yes – Sat–Mon |
| Oct 9 | Thanksgiving | Mon | Yes – Sat–Mon |
| Nov 20 | Remembrance Day | Mon | Yes – Sat–Mon |
| Dec 25 | Christmas Day | Mon | Yes – Sat–Mon |
| Dec 26 | Boxing Day | Tue | Yes – Mon–Tue |

**Quick note:**  
* Some provinces observe additional holidays (e.g., Family Day in Alberta on the third Monday of February, St. Patrick’s Day in Newfoundland & Labrador on March 17, etc.).  
* If you’re looking at specific provinces or territories, let me know which one(s), and I can tailor the list accordingly.

Would you like a more detailed breakdown for a particular province or territory?
